blocks.h2: Reasons to Get a Sewer Camera Inspection in Elgin

tiles.body: An 1800s or early 1900s house near downtown almost always has an old lateral. Look before you close.
If you're calling for rodding more than once a year, the camera tells you whether a repair would end it.
Was it your line or an overloaded sewer? The footage answers that.
Check the line and the drains under the floor before new finishes go in.

blocks.h2: What We Find in Elgin Sewer Lines
blocks.intro: Elgin's housing ranges from the 1800s to the 2000s, so the footage varies a lot from street to street.

items.h3: Roots and Offset Joints in Clay
items.body: The most common finding east of the river. Short clay sections shift over time, and roots move in at the gaps.
Many historic-area lines show sections replaced decades ago with a different material. The transitions are worth a close look.
On the west side, the camera often finds a low spot where soil settled after construction.
Sometimes the pipe is fine and the problem is what's been going down it. That's good news.

items.h3: Buying on Either Side of the River
items.body: East side homes tend to show old clay and patches. West side homes tend to show sags and grease. Either way, the camera shows you before you buy.

blocks.h2: How a Camera Inspection Works With Us

steps.body: No digging and no opening walls.
We mark the spot and depth of any problem from above.
We explain what matters, what doesn't and what to do next, and you keep the video.

blocks.h2: Sewer Camera Questions From Elgin Homeowners

items.q: Should I inspect the sewer before buying a home in Elgin?
items.answer: Yes. A standard home inspection doesn't look inside the sewer. For a home built before about 1980, and especially one in the historic districts, a camera inspection can reveal a costly repair before you close.

items.preview: We can often go through a roof vent or toilet, or add a cleanout.
items.answer: We may be able to go in through a roof vent or by pulling a toilet. If access is poor, adding a cleanout makes future inspections and cleanings much easier.

items.q: Can you tell how deep the problem is?
items.preview: Yes. The locator gives depth and position.
items.answer: Yes. The camera head carries a transmitter, and our locator shows where it is and how deep, so a repair can be targeted.

items.q: Do I get a copy of the video?
items.answer: Yes. You keep the recording for your records, a buyer or a seller.

items.q: How long does a sewer camera inspection take?
items.preview: About an hour for most homes.
items.answer: About an hour for most homes, including setup and walking you through the footage.

items.q: How much does a sewer camera inspection cost in Elgin?
items.preview: It depends on access and line length. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on access and how long the line is. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
